title.narrative: Supporting Innovation in the Philippine Technical and Vocational Education and Training System Project

description.narrative: The project will support modernizing the Philippine technical and vocational education and training (TVET) system, so that it can respond effectively to an increasingly globalized, technology- and knowledge-driven market. It will improve the quality of skilling programs, upgrade training facilities and equipment, and build the capacity of trainers to impart the higher-level skills and competencies demanded by the job market. The project will help the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), the Philippine TVET agency, to undertake institutional reforms and forge stronger engagement between public TVET institutions and industry, thereby enhancing the employability of Filipino youth and workers. It will also support the government's National Employment Recovery Strategy (NERS) to help the economy bounce back from the adverse effects of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19).

Output: TESDA's institutional capacity strengthened Indicator: Increased knowledge of at least 88 TESDA staff (of whom at least 50% are women) and at least 51 trainers and administrators of the 17 TTIs on ADB's gender and development, financial management, procurement, climate assessment, and safeguards policies Progress/Status: During Q2 2026, the SIPTVETS Project successfully completed the regional workshops on Gender Equality, Environmental, and Social Safeguards, reaching 107 participants, 74 (69.16%) of whom were female. Output: TVET made more demand-driven and industry-led Indicator: 34 new partnership agreements signed by the 17 TTIs (including their RTICs) with industry partners and LGUs Progress/Status: 7 MOUs have been signed with the ff RTICs:
● Regional Training Center - National Capital Region (RTC-NCR) ● Gonzalo Puyat School of Arts and Trades (GPSAT-R03) ● Provincial Training Center Rosario (PTC Rosario- R4A) ● Simeon Suan Vocational and Technical College (SSVTC-R4B) ● Regional Training Center Zamboanga (RTC - R11) ● Regional Training Center Tagoloan (RTC-R10) ● General Santos National School of Arts & Trades (GNSAT-R12)
New partnerships are being explored in the other TTIs
In addition to the seven (7) MOUs signed in 2025, the project is actively pursuing new partnerships across the remaining TTIs to achieve the target of twenty-seven (27) additional MOUs/partnership agreements. Ongoing engagement with industry partners, government agencies, and other stakeholders aims to strengthen collaboration, expand training and employment opportunities, and support the delivery of industry-responsive skills development programs. Data Source: MOAs, MOUs, and TTIs' annual operations reports; compendium of TVET-registered programs Actual value:

Output: The Philippines' skills development ecosystem modernized Indicator: 21 new training regulations and/or competency standards reflecting gender and green or climate mainstreaming principles and imparting 4IR skills and competencies introduced Progress/Status: Nine (9) competency standards (CS) were drafted by the three consultants engaged for mechatronics, warehousing, and farm mechanization. These CS were validated in a workshop held on 15-17 April 2026, which was attended by 63 participants, of whom 40% were female. This activity marked the continuation of the October 2025 functional analysis, ensuring that draft CS were aligned with industry requirements and stakeholders' expectations.
In further strengthening the responsiveness of the TVET system to future workforce requirements, an Exploratory Dialogue on Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) CS was conducted on 3 June 2026 at the TESDA Women's Center, Taguig City. The activity brought together 42 experts from industry, academe, Local Government Units, Asian Development Bank (ADB) and TESDA Executive Offices, 60% of whom were female, to identify emerging competencies and technologies that should bee integrated into future competency standards. This dialogue provided key technical inputs for integrating 4IR skills into competency frameworks, ensuring that TESDA training regulations remain relevant to evolving industry needs and technological advancements.
Recruitment process for the consultants for (i) SMART Fish Culture with Advanced Post-Harvest Operations, (ii) Precision Engineering supporting Welding Technology, Metal Fabrication and Additive Technology, (iii) Refrigeration and Cold Chain, (iv) Welding Technology to support Farm Mechanization and Construction, and (v) Automotive Technology in support to Logistic Requirements of Agriculture Industry, are ongoing.
Data Source: TESDA training regulations and/or competency standards Actual value:

Output: The Philippines' skills development ecosystem modernized Indicator: 51 new and/or updated gender-responsive and socially inclusive TOP courses developed and introduced Progress/Status: TESDA engaged consultant, Ms. Ambrosio, completed the evaluation of the effectiveness of the TESDA Online Proggram (TOP) for enhanced eLearning delivery to be adopted by the 17 RTICs on 13 December 205. The evaluation provides the evidence base for the updating and development of TOP courses.
Building on the findings of the evaluation, eTESDA will proceed with the development of the first batch of 17 TOP courses carried over from the previous year, with emphasis on integrating 21st-century skills into the learning content. Course development will continue through the Q4 2026. The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this activity are currently in the final stages of preparation.
To support the timely and accelerated development of the remaining 34 TOP courses targeted for 2027, eTESDA, with technical assistance from the PMC, will begin preparatory activities in the Q3 this year. These early preparations are intended to streamline implementation, strengthen coordination, and ensure that course development proceeds according to the planned schedule. Data Source: List of programs in TOP's TVET compendium Actual value:

To date, 8 RTICs were awarded with progress as of 30 June 2026: ● Region II - Tuguegarao - 43.32% ● Region VIII- Tacloban - 18.95% ● Region XII- GenSan - 17.93% ● NCR - Taguig -14.96% ● Region VI - Iloilo - 12.29% ● Region X- Tagoloan - 8.4% ● Region IX Zamboanga - 0% ● Region XIII NMSF Caraga -0%
The civil works contractors for both the Zamboanga and CARAGA project sites are still at the preparatory and mobilization phase after receipt of Notice of Award on 04 March 2026, followed by the Notice to Proceed on 12 March 2026.
EQUIPMENT: The G101-A procurement for multimedia equipment for the Innovation Centers and the eTESDA PMU has substantially progressed. Lot 2, covering 18 units of software, was awarded to World Solution Technology on 2 September 2025 and was completed on 3 November 2025. Lot 1, covering 270 units for 17 TTIs and the eTESDA Central Office (15 units each), was awarded to ACMI on 4 September 2025, with delivery successfully completed on 31 December 2025. Testing and installation for Lot 1 was scheduled for completion by 31 January 2026, in accordance with the ADB-approved contract extension granted on 18 December 2025
The G304-A procurement for IT Equipment for existing TTIs for digital learning, Hybrid Training, Security & Monitoring, and Networking Infrastructure is ongoing procurement, with bid submission and opening on 13 April 2026.
The G305-A procurement for IT Equipment for Batch 1 & 2 RTICs is currently undergoing evaluation of the 8 sites—RTC - Iloilo, RTC - Tuguegarao, RTC - NCR, RTC - Tacloban, General Santos School of Arts and Trades, Northern Mindanao School of Fisheries, RTC - Zamboanga, and RTC - Tagoloan—by the Information and Communications Technology Office (ICTO) to gather data for the drafting of the Terms of Reference (TOR)
For the procurement of training and innovation equipment, the NITESD and TWG in collaboration with the PMC, and the ADB as Resource Persons held a 2-day orientation/workshop to kick-off the preparation of the Terms of Reference/specifications for the upgrading of the equipment of existing TTIs and new equipment for the RTICs. In this quarter, industry site visits were conducted as part of the early market engagement activity and market scoping. The first batch of specifications are targeted to be completed in Q2/2026.

Output: The Philippines' skills development ecosystem modernized Indicator: Career counseling and placement services updated in line with industry needs and made more gender-responsive, socially inclusive, and culturally appropriate Progress/Status: Final report on the newly developed Career Profiling Instrument (CPI) was submitted by the contracted consultant from Inno-Change International Consultants, Inc to PMO in June 2026. Based on the submitted CPI report, initial training on the CPI administration, interpretation, recording of test results, and its application in the career guidance program and services was conducted. The final Manual of Test Administration is needed to deepen its integration to the broader career guidance counseling competencies of the guidance counselor/career advocates/focal persons in the 17 TTIs. The capability-building activities will address this goal.
Initial training on the administration and interpretation of the CPI was conducted. However, specific capability building activities will address its integration to the broader career guidance counseling competencies of the guidance counselor/career advocates/focal persons in the SIPTVETS TTIs.
